purpose: Ask Vetri is a citizen assistant. It takes one free-text sentence in Tamil, English or both, works out which government services that life situation needs, puts them in dependency order (what has to come first), and returns three things: a Tamil headline, an English explanation built from the service catalogue (fee, processing time, why this step comes here), and up to 4 clickable cards that open the real service application. It also shows up to 4 proactive suggestions worked out from the citizen's own records (an expired certificate, age-based next steps, the property-tax rebate window, number of eligible schemes). It is deterministic code, not an LLM. docs/PHASE4.md line 13 says so directly: "this build runs fully offline with no live LLM, so the pipeline is deterministic reasoning". All of the life-event reasoning below runs in the frontend engine through the offline MSW mock backend (VITE_ENABLE_MSW=true, which is the 'vetri-offline' launch config and the mode used for every capture). The NestJS backend has its own, much simpler keyword AI.

capabilities.name: 5-stage deterministic pipeline (runAskVetri)
capabilities.what_it_really_does: orchestrator.ts runAskVetri(text, raw, memory) runs extractIntent → buildContext → buildPlan → executePlan → compose, in that order. The stage names in the code comment and PHASE4.md are, verbatim: 'text → Intent Engine → Citizen Context → Planning Engine → Tool Orchestrator → Response Composer → reply (+ visible plan trace)', supported by 'Government Knowledge Graph + Life Event Engine + Memory'. Every stage is plain typed data: IntentFrame → CitizenContext → Plan{goal, steps[{tool, rationale}]} → ToolResult[] → ComposedReply{text, en, actions, plan, intent}. The MSW handler is a thin delegate: POST /api/ai/chat calls runAskVetri(text, rawState(), memory) with rawState = db.citizen, db.documents, the application records, db.schemes and the unread-notification count.
capabilities.visual_potential: A horizontal 5-node pipeline (Intent Engine, Citizen Context, Planning Engine, Tool Orchestrator, Response Composer) with the citizen's sentence flowing in on the left and the Tamil headline plus cards coming out on the right. The knowledge layer (Knowledge Graph, Life Event Engine, Memory) sits underneath and feeds up into the planner. Label it 'deterministic reasoning engine', not 'AI model'.

capabilities.name: Intent Engine: multi-event extraction from one sentence
capabilities.what_it_really_does: extractIntent() regex-matches the text against life-event triggers (en + ta) and a keyword index of 21 services. It returns ALL matching life events, in LIFE_EVENTS array order (not the order they appear in the sentence), plus language (en/ta/mixed via Tamil Unicode range), district entity (TN_DISTRICTS), reference numbers (APP|CMP|CRT-YYYY-XX-n), sentiment (empathetic/celebratory from event tone) and urgency. Kind precedence: lifeEvent > trackStatus > coverageQuery > documentQuery > schemeQuery > timelineQuery > apply/explainService > payment > navigate > smalltalk. Verified by actually running the code: 'I moved to Chennai after marriage and bought a house' → {kind:'lifeEvent', lifeEvents:['marriage','propertyPurchase','migration'], entities:{district:'Chennai'}, sentiment:'celebratory', language:'en'}. Tamil 'நான் நிலம் வாங்கினேன்' → lifeEvent propertyPurchase, language 'ta'.
capabilities.visual_potential: Type the sentence, then highlight the three trigger fragments as they match: 'moved to' → Migration, 'marri(age)' → Marriage, 'bought a house' → Property purchase. Each fragment lifts off as a chip carrying its Tamil label (இடமாற்றம், திருமணம், சொத்து வாங்குதல்). 'Chennai' gets tagged as a district entity.

capabilities.name: Life Event Engine: 9 events with dependency-ordered service sequences
capabilities.what_it_really_does: LIFE_EVENTS holds 9 nodes. Each has en/ta labels, triggers, a tone, an ORDERED services[] list where the order encodes the dependencies, per-service dependency notes, and benefits. The composer walks each matched event's services in order, de-duplicates services across events (the first event's dependency note wins), and numbers them 1..N. Sequences, verbatim ids with resolved catalogue names: (1) bereavement 'Death in the family'/'குடும்பத்தில் இழப்பு' [empathetic]: svc_death Death Certificate → svc_legalheir Legal Heir Certificate → svc_patta Patta Transfer → svc_ration Ration Card (Smart Card). (2) marriage 'Marriage'/'திருமணம்' [celebratory]: svc_marriage Marriage Certificate → svc_ration Ration Card (Smart Card) → svc_residence Residence Certificate. (3) propertyPurchase 'Property / land purchase'/'சொத்து வாங்குதல்' [neutral]: svc_ec Encumbrance Certificate → svc_chitta Chitta / Patta Extract → svc_patta Patta Transfer → svc_proptax Property Tax Payment → svc_water Water Charges. (4) migration 'Moving / address change'/'இடமாற்றம்': svc_dl Driving Licence → svc_ration Ration Card (Smart Card) → svc_residence Residence Certificate. (5) birth 'New baby'/'குழந்தை பிறப்பு' [celebratory]: svc_birth Birth Certificate → svc_ration Ration Card (Smart Card). (6) vehiclePurchase 'Vehicle purchase'/'வாகனம் வாங்குதல்': svc_rctransfer RC Transfer → svc_echallan e-Challan Payment → svc_mvtax Vehicle Tax Payment. (7) education 'School / college admission'/'கல்வி சேர்க்கை': svc_nativity Nativity Certificate → svc_income Income Certificate → svc_community Community Certificate → svc_residence Residence Certificate. (8) retirement 'Retirement / senior citizen'/'ஓய்வு': svc_income Income Certificate → svc_legalheir Legal Heir Certificate. (9) farming 'Farming / agriculture'/'விவசாயம்': svc_adangal Adangal Extract (A-Register) → svc_chitta Chitta / Patta Extract → svc_patta Patta Transfer.
capabilities.visual_potential: A constellation of 9 life-event nodes with Tamil labels. When one lights up it unfolds into its ordered chain of service tiles, joined by arrows annotated with the real dependency note, for example 'needs the Death Certificate first'. For the combined sentence, three chains merge and the duplicates (Ration Card, Residence Certificate) collapse into single tiles.

capabilities.name: Government Knowledge Graph (derived from the real service catalogue)
capabilities.what_it_really_does: SERVICE_GRAPH is built when the module loads from SERVICE_META + FORMS (21 services). Each node has meta (name, nameTamil, fee, processingTime, authorities.issuing), document requirements, a keyword regex (en + ta), up to 5 related services (EXTRA_EDGES plus services that share a life event), and curated tips, commonMistakes and rejectionReasons. The fees and times in replies come straight from meta.ts, e.g. Encumbrance Certificate '₹116 + ₹5/yr', '2–5 working days', issuing 'Sub-Registrar (SRO)'.
capabilities.visual_potential: A network graph of the 21 services with edges such as EC→Chitta→Patta→Property Tax. Hover cards show the real fee and SLA, e.g. 'Patta Transfer · ₹60 (transfer) · Full/Joint: 15 days'.

capabilities.name: Planning Engine + visible reasoning trace
capabilities.what_it_really_does: buildPlan() never answers. It emits typed tool steps, and each step's rationale string becomes the 'plan' trace line. For lifeEvent the steps are: wallet.list 'Check which documents the citizen already holds', applications.list 'Check for in-flight applications to avoid duplicates', then one service.meta 'Expand the {eventId} event into its service sequence' per event, then navigate.build 'Prepare one action per recommended service'. The trace is returned in the API reply ('plan') and rendered ONLY in the Mobile Super App bubble (AIAssistant.jsx): 10px muted lines, each with a 9px green CheckCircle, above the Tamil text. DesktopAI.tsx drops reply.plan, so the desktop portal shows no trace.
capabilities.visual_potential: Checklist ticks appearing one by one: ✓ Check which documents the citizen already holds / ✓ Check for in-flight applications to avoid duplicates / ✓ Expand the marriage event... / ✓ Expand the propertyPurchase event... / ✓ Expand the migration event... / ✓ Prepare one action per recommended service. This is accurate to the Mobile Super App UI. On a desktop shot it has to be labelled as an overlay of the engine's real plan output.

capabilities.name: Tool Orchestrator (8-tool registry)
capabilities.what_it_really_does: executePlan() dispatches to pure functions over the citizen context: 'wallet.list', 'wallet.coverage' (regex-matches the service's FORMS checklist against wallet documents and returns covered/requiredTotal/missing, with expiry detection from MM/YYYY validity), 'applications.list', 'applications.forService' (duplicate detection: active apps for that service), 'service.meta', 'schemes.match', 'timeline.predict' (future-need prediction), 'navigate.build'. Verified output for 'I need an income certificate': 'You already have APP-2026-IC-44821 in progress (In Progress) — track it instead of re-applying. Your Wallet already covers 3 of 5 required documents ... ⚠ Income Proof (Salary slip / IT return / PAN) (your Income Certificate IC-TN-2024-9912 has EXPIRED).'
capabilities.visual_potential: Tool-call pills (wallet.coverage, applications.forService) firing against the citizen's real wallet cards (DL-TN-2024-8842, BC-TN-2002-4421, IC-TN-2024-9912 stamped EXPIRED, RC-TN-CHN-7788). The duplicate-detection beat lands on the live reference APP-2026-IC-44821.

capabilities.name: Response Composer: bilingual reply + action cards
capabilities.what_it_really_does: compose() builds the Tamil headline from a per-intent template (lifeEvent: '{labelTamil joined by " + "} — தேவையான சேவைகளை வரிசைப்படுத்தியுள்ளேன்:'). The English body starts with a tone prefix ('Congratulations! ' for celebratory, 'My deepest condolences. I will handle the paperwork so you don’t have to think about it. ' for empathetic) and continues with numbered '{n}. {name} ({fee}, {processingTime}) — {dependency}', then 'Also check: {benefits}.', then 'I sequenced these by dependency — start from the top. Your Wallet already holds 4 verified documents I can reuse across these.' Action cards are service cards {label: meta.name, screen: 'service/{id}', kind:'apply'}, capped at 4. Clicking one navigates to the real /service/:id application flow.
capabilities.visual_potential: The Tamil headline types on first (the hero line), the English steps cascade beneath, then 4 crimson-outlined pill buttons with arrow icons slide in. Click 'Encumbrance Certificate →' and cut to the real service form.

capabilities.name: Proactive suggestions (computeProactive)
capabilities.what_it_really_does: GET /api/ai/suggestions runs timeline.predict over live state and returns the first 4 predictions. Rules: every expired wallet document → '{name} ({number}) has expired — renewal recommended'; pending corrections; no DL and age>=18; age>=21 with no marriage document; a date-aware property-tax line (OPEN in April/October, otherwise 'opens April 1'/'opens October 1'); scheme count. For the demo citizen (DOB 22 May 2002, holds a DL, IC expired 03/2025, 9 schemes) in October the 4 lines are exactly as captured in citizen__ai.png. Desktop shows them under 'Suggested for you' with Lightbulb icons. Mobile shows them as chips under 'Ask Vetri noticed', only before the first message.
capabilities.visual_potential: The four suggestion rows fade in one by one in the right rail. The expired-certificate number and the 'OPEN' rebate window are the strongest 'it already knows me' beats.

capabilities.name: Citizen memory + voice (Mobile Super App only)
capabilities.what_it_really_does: useCitizenMemory (zustand persist key 'vetri.ai.memory') counts service-card taps and the last 10 intents. The intent engine re-sorts matched services by tap count. Only AIAssistant.jsx sends memory.snapshot() and records taps; DesktopAI does neither. Voice uses the browser Web Speech API (rec.lang 'ta-IN' or 'en-IN' from the UI language). Starting the mic or sending a new message cancels any TTS in progress, and replies to voice input are spoken aloud. The transcript persists separately under 'vetri.ai' (last 30 messages).
capabilities.visual_potential: Mobile phone frame: tap the mic, the header status changes 'Online' → 'Listening…', speak Tamil, the reply is read aloud. Only the mobile experience can show this; the desktop page has no mic.

honesty_flags: NO LIVE LLM. docs/PHASE4.md line 13: 'this build runs fully offline with no live LLM, so the pipeline is deterministic reasoning'. Matching is regex triggers plus keyword indexes; the replies are filled-in templates (the composer interpolates catalogue data into fixed sentence patterns such as 'I sequenced these by dependency — start from the top.'). Do not call it generative AI, a language model, or 'understanding'. 'Deterministic reasoning engine' / 'rule-based life-event engine' is accurate. responseComposer.ts is the documented place a model could be swapped in later; that is a roadmap item, not something that exists.

TWO DIFFERENT BACKENDS. The life-event engine runs only in the frontend through MSW (offline mode, VITE_ENABLE_MSW=true, the 'vetri-offline' launch config used for every capture). The repo's .env.local defaults to the NestJS backend (VITE_ENABLE_MSW=false), and backend/src/modules/ai/ai.service.ts is a simpler keyword classifier (intents greeting/track/wallet/apply/scheme/complaint/help/fallback) with no life events. In that mode 'I bought land' and the marriage/house sentence both fall to the 'fallback' reply: 'I want to make sure I help correctly, ...'. Film only the offline/MSW behaviour, and do not claim the server runs the life-event engine. backend/src/ai/ is an empty directory.

The desktop portal (DesktopAI.tsx) does NOT render the reasoning trace. It discards reply.plan and shows only the Tamil headline (14px), English body (12.5px, 72% opacity) and action buttons. The ✓ trace exists only in the Mobile Super App (AIAssistant.jsx). Any desktop shot with trace lines is a composited overlay of real engine output and should not be presented as the desktop UI.

PHASE4.md is out of date on the flagship example. It says '7-step merged plan ... 3 action cards' (Marriage → Ration → Residence → EC → Chitta → Patta → Property Tax). The current code produces 9 numbered steps (it adds Water Charges and Driving Licence) and 4 action cards, and the capture matches the code. Quote the code/capture, not the doc.

The English reply renders as one dense run-on paragraph (numbering inline, '1. … 2. …', no line breaks). Laying it out as a vertical list in the film reformats the text; the content is real but the layout is not the app's. The 4-card cap means steps 5–9 have no cards.
Life events are listed in LIFE_EVENTS array order, not the order the user mentions them. 'moved to Chennai after marriage' still yields marriage → property → migration.

Some trace lines overstate what happens. For life events, the 'Check for in-flight applications to avoid duplicates' result is never consulted by the composer (no dedup against live apps on this path). The 'wallet.list' result is used only as a count ('Your Wallet already holds 4 verified documents'), and that count includes the expired Income Certificate. Real duplicate detection exists only on the single-service path (applyService/coverageQuery).

Computed but never shown: entities.district ('Chennai' is extracted but unused), urgency, futureRecommendations and rejectionReasons. Do not show 'Vetri recommends next: Voter-ID update…' etc. as on-screen output.

Scheme 'match %' values (e.g. PM Kisan Samman Nidhi 95%, Annanin Seer Scheme 92%) are static seed values in schemes2026.ts. schemes.match just returns ctx.schemes and does no scoring. 'Eligible for 9 welfare schemes' is simply the length of the catalogue.

Clicking the suggestion rows sends generic prompts ('Help me with income', 'Help me with proptax') that resolve to the smalltalk intent and a generic reply ('நான் உங்கள் அரசு உதவியாளர். இவை உதவலாம்:' + 'I can start any government service…'). The Try-asking chip 'What documents are in my locker?' also falls to smalltalk. Do not film these as targeted answers. 'Help me with marriage' does trigger the marriage life event.

The suggestions depend on the date: 'window is OPEN' appears only in April/October (the capture was taken in October). Rendering live in another month changes the line to 'opens April 1' or 'opens October 1'.

subsystem: Governance portals + transparency (Officer, Department, MLA, Super Admin, citizen District Scorecard / MLA Dashboard, analytics API, chart kit)
purpose:
This is the government-facing side of Vetri TN. One login screen (/demo, titled "Presentation Mode") lets you enter as any of five roles: Citizen, Officer, Department, MLA or Super Admin. Each role lands in a portal protected by role-based permissions (RBAC).
- An Officer works a queue of citizen applications. Approve, Reject, Correction, Escalate and Transfer are all legal moves in the workflow engine, and every move writes an audit entry and sends the citizen a notification.
- A Department head sees an operational dashboard.
- An MLA sees analytics for their constituency (Mylapore), split into five sections, with a ward heat map and an auto-advancing presentation mode.
- The Super Admin sees platform counts, the health of 14 integration adapters, feature flags, a broadcast form, client logs and the audit trail.
- Citizens get read-only transparency pages (/district, /mla) built from the same analytics data.
In the offline build every number comes from MSW mock handlers. They are seeded "charter-plausible" figures plus a small live offset taken from the 2 seeded applications.

subsystem: Citizen service journey: catalogue → apply → track → certificate in Digital Locker, plus home, timeline, schemes, grievances, emergency, notifications
purpose: This is the citizen's working path through the desktop portal. A signed-in citizen (persona "Chandramoulishwarar K", Citizen ID TN-2024-XXXX-8842) browses 21 official TN services and applies through a stepper driven by data definitions (Form Engine). The submission gets an APP-2026-XX-NNNNN reference and a scannable QR, and its progress through the 13-stage 'gov.standard.v1' Right-to-Service workflow shows on the tracker with the assigned officer. When an officer approves it in the Officer Portal, a CRT- certificate is placed in the citizen's Digital Locker automatically and a notification is sent. Alongside this sit a lifetime Digital Citizen Timeline, 9 welfare schemes ranked by match % with Tamil names, a grievance form that previews department routing live and issues a CMP- reference, an emergency number directory and a notification inbox. All screenshots run on in-browser MSW mocks (VITE_ENABLE_MSW=true). The NestJS backend uses the same reference formats (backend/src/modules/applications/applications.service.ts:46, complaints.service.ts:36).

capabilities.name: Government Workflow Engine 'gov.standard.v1' (13-stage Right-to-Service pipeline)
capabilities.what_it_really_does: A data-defined state machine with 15 stage definitions and a legal-transition adjacency list. Happy path (13): Submitted → Document Verification → Officer Assigned → Department Queue → Inspection → Remarks → Approval → Digital Signature → Certificate Generation → Delivered to Wallet → Citizen Notified → Completed. Branches: Escalation (from Inspection, leads to Approval or Rejected), Rejected (terminal), Correction Requested (loops back to Document Verification). Actors are citizen/system/officer/department/signatory. Stage SLAs: Document Verification 1 day, Inspection 3, Approval 2. applyTransition throws on illegal moves. Officer actions reach their targets by BFS over legal transitions. The citizen-facing status label maps most stages to 'In Progress', plus 'Escalated', 'Completed', 'Rejected', 'Correction Requested'.

subsystem: Platform architecture and scale facts (backend/, src/lib/{integrations,rbac,api,workflow}, docs/*.md)
purpose: Vetri Tamil Nadu is one citizen-services platform. A resident signs in with one identity and can apply for 21 Tamil Nadu government services. Every application, whatever the service, moves through the same config-driven workflow (gov.standard.v1, 15 stages). The system assigns an officer in the citizen's district, the officer approves or acts on it in a portal, and the issued certificate goes into the citizen's digital wallet with a notification and a timeline entry. Department, MLA and Admin portals sit on the same data and are separated by RBAC. External government systems sit behind a typed Integration Gateway: 14 capabilities on the frontend and 10 adapters on the backend, all in mock mode today. The frontend is React 19 + Vite 8 and runs fully offline on MSW mocks. The NestJS 10 + Postgres 16/Prisma 5 backend has identical contracts, so going live is a change to the env seam (config/env.ts). Recommended one-sentence definition: "Vetri Tamil Nadu is a working prototype of a unified Tamil Nadu government services platform. One citizen identity reaches 21 state services, and every application runs through a single 15-stage government workflow from citizen to officer to department, ending with a certificate in the citizen's digital wallet. Officers, departments, MLAs and administrators each get their own role-based portal, and the government-system integrations are mocked today." The real-world problem it addresses is only stated qualitatively in code and docs; there are no problem statistics in the repo. Supporting quotes: DesktopLogin.tsx says "apply, track and receive government services without visiting an office". OnboardingScreen.jsx has the cards "One Citizen Identity", "Every Service, One Tap", "Track Everything" and "No Middlemen — Direct access. Transparent timelines. Officer accountability." PHASE2.md has "one platform, all departments". The catalog itself shows the fragmentation: the 21 services carry 12 distinct department labels, and 9 of them are 'assisted' services that hand off to separate official portals (parivahan.gov.in, tnpds.gov.in, eservices.tn.gov.in/TamilNilam, tnreginet.gov.in). On paperwork, meta.ts ESIGN_NOTE says "Digitally signed PDFs carry full legal validity under the IT Act, 2000 — no physical stamp needed", and wallet documents can be reused as attachments. What makes it state-scale (architecturally, not in deployment): (1) the 38 real TN districts are encoded, with a District→Taluk→Village hierarchy in Postgres; (2) one workflow definition serves every service, so adding a service is configuration only (Phase 3.5 added 13 services with 0 routes, 0 APIs and 0 components); (3) one RBAC catalog gates 5 portals; (4) one gateway interface fronts every external system; (5) officer assignment is load-aware by the citizen's district; (6) every mutating request writes an audit-log entry; (7) the platform is bilingual Tamil/English.

capabilities.name: Single config-driven Government Workflow Engine (gov.standard.v1)
capabilities.what_it_really_does: There are 15 stages in total: submitted, docVerification, officerAssigned, departmentQueue, inspection, remarks, escalation, approval, digitalSignature, certificateGeneration, walletDelivery, notified, completed, rejected, correctionRequested. The primary path has 12 stages: submitted→Document Verification→Officer Assigned→Department Queue→Inspection→Remarks→Approval→Digital Signature→Certificate Generation→Delivered to Wallet→Citizen Notified→Completed. Escalation, Correction Requested and Rejected are branches off it. Each stage has an actor (citizen, system, department, officer or signatory) and SLAs are set on some stages (docVerification 1 day, inspection 3, approval 2). Officer actions find a legal path by BFS over the transition graph instead of jumping state. When an application reaches walletDelivery, the backend creates a CRT-numbered Document, a 'Certificate Ready' notification and a timeline event. The same definition exists in the frontend (lib/workflow) and the backend (workflow.engine.ts), is seeded as Workflow/WorkflowStep rows, and is used by every service (workflowId default 'gov.standard.v1').

capabilities.name: Backend API surface and hardening
capabilities.what_it_really_does: 34 HTTP endpoints: 31 business routes under /api, 2 gateway routes and /health, plus Swagger at /api/docs. There are 13 module directories (auth, workflow, applications, catalog, documents, notifications, citizen, officer, analytics, complaints, search, ai, health) plus the Prisma and Integrations modules. Hardening: JWT access tokens (default TTL 900 s) with rotating refresh tokens (default 1,209,600 s, i.e. 14 days); bcrypt-hashed OTPs that expire after 5 minutes; Helmet; a throttle of 120 requests per 60 s; pino logs that redact the authorization header, OTP and refresh token; AllExceptionsFilter returning normalised { statusCode, message, fieldErrors, path, timestamp }; and a Docker Compose stack of postgres, redis, backend and pgadmin. The frontend lib/api client adds timeouts, exponential-backoff retry, 401→refresh→retry, Zod validation of every response, and a normalised ApiError.

Dashboard and analytics figures are seeded demo aggregates, not government statistics. Seed volumes (1,001 citizens, 500 applications, 200 complaints, 100 officers) are synthetic demo data generated from 20 first names × 10 last names. They are not real records and not a measure of capacity.

Service count is inconsistent across layers. The frontend catalog and Admin tile say 21, the backend seed has 20 with a different mix (it includes Old Age Pension and Hospital Appointment and omits Adangal, FMB and e-Challan), and the login says '20+'. Use '21 services' only when referring to the shown portal, or '20+'. Do not claim '100+ services'.

Only 12 of the 21 services complete inside Vetri with a certificate to the wallet (mode 'digital'). The other 9 are 'assisted': Driving Licence, Ration Card, Patta Transfer, RC Transfer, Duplicate RC, Vehicle Tax, e-Challan, Property Tax and Water Charges. They collect and prefill data and then hand off to Parivahan, TNPDS, TamilNilam or a ULB portal. Do not say 'all services end-to-end in one app'.

Welfare scheme count is 9, not 100. The backend README line '100 welfare schemes' is stale; seed.ts now seeds 9 with 'no padding'. Scheme budgets (₹812 Cr, ₹560 Cr, ₹2,000 Cr, ₹777 Cr, about ₹4,149 Cr across 4 schemes) are flagged in schemes2026.ts as supplied by the product owner and 'have not been re-verified against the published budget document'. Do not present them as verified. The '9 Eligible Schemes' hero tile is the catalogue count, not a computed eligibility result.

Integration count conflicts. The Admin Overview shows 14 (frontend capabilities, with TNeGA reusing the e-Sevai mock), the backend has 10, the Admin 'Manage' tab hardcodes '11 registered', and docs cite 11 (Phase 1) then 14 (Phase 3). Pick one and attribute it, e.g. '14 integration adapters (mock)' on the frontend admin screen.
Roles: say 5 (frontend portals). The backend enum has 6 (SUPPORT), but SUPPORT has no portal or route.

AI is not an LLM. Ask Vetri is a deterministic intent→plan→tools→compose pipeline (PHASE4.md honesty note: 'no live LLM'). The backend AI service uses regex intent rules. Do not say 'powered by generative AI' or 'understands any question'.

OTP and SMS are not sent. The backend uses a fixed OTP of '123456' in mock mode, MSW accepts any 6 digits, and biometric login is a one-tap mock. The login copy 'We will send a one-time password to your Aadhaar-linked mobile number' describes intended behaviour. Also, 'Vetri never stores your Aadhaar number or OTP' is loose: the DB stores aadhaarMasked and a bcrypt OTP hash.

Payments are not processed. The service-flow Payment step only records the chosen method ('no card or UPI credentials are captured here'). The Payment model exists, but there is no payment endpoint. Do not claim 'pay fees online'.

No backend document storage. The upload UI validates and previews client-side, but there is no upload endpoint (the Attachment model is unused by the API). eSign and 'Digital Signature' is a workflow stage with a mock adapter, not a real DSC. Certificates are records, not generated signed PDFs (server-side PDF generation is listed as remaining work in PHASE2.md).
Redis and BullMQ are installed and in docker-compose, but no queues are implemented ('queues-ready'; backend/src/jobs is an empty directory). Do not claim async job processing or scale-out.
Notifications are in-app only. The SMS, email and push adapters are mocks, and Admin 'Broadcast' writes in-app notification rows.

'Official' branding: the UI banner reads 'Government of Tamil Nadu · Official Citizen Services Portal' and uses the state seal, and the login says 'The official digital gateway of the Government of Tamil Nadu'. This is a pitch prototype for a Minister, not an officially sanctioned portal. The film should not assert official status or government endorsement.

There are no problem statistics in the repo (no counts of offices, visits, days saved, middlemen, or paperwork reduction). Any quantified 'before/after' claim would be invented. Only the qualitative framing quoted from DesktopLogin.tsx, OnboardingScreen.jsx and PHASE2.md is supported.
